sanskrit: uṣitvā rajanīṃ tatra rājaputrāv ariṃdamau maharṣim abhivādyātha jagmatus taṃ giriṃ prati
english: Having spent the night there, the two princes, those tamers of foes, saluted the great sage and then set out toward that mountain.

sanskrit: prasthitāṃś caiva tān prekṣya pitā putrān ivānvagāt tataḥ pracakrame vaktuṃ vacanaṃ sa mahāmuniḥ
english: Watching them depart, he followed after them as a father follows his sons; then that great sage began to speak these words.

sanskrit: athāsādya tu kālindīṃ śīghrasrotasamāpagām tatra yūyaṃ plavaṃ kṛtvā taratāṃśumatīṃ nadīm
english: "When you reach the Kālindī, the swiftly flowing river, there you must build a raft and cross the river Aṃśumatī."

sanskrit: tato nyagrodham āsādya mahāntaṃ haritacchadam vivṛddhaṃ bahubhir vṛkṣaiḥ śyāmaṃ siddhopasevitam
english: "Then, having reached the great banyan tree with its green canopy, grown tall amid many trees, dark and frequented by siddhas —"

sanskrit: krośamātraṃ tato gatvā nīlaṃ drakṣyatha kānanam palāśabadarīmiśraṃ rāma vaṃśaiś ca yāmunaiḥ
english: "— having gone just one krośa from there, O Rāma, you will see a dark forest, mixed with palāśa trees, badara shrubs, and the bamboo groves of the Yamunā."

sanskrit: sa panthāś citrakūṭasya gataḥ subahuśo mayā ramyo mārdavayuktaś ca vanadāvair vivarjitaḥ iti panthānam āvedya maharṣiḥ sa nyavartata
english: "That is the path to Citrakūṭa, which I have traversed many times — pleasant, gentle underfoot, and free of forest fires." Having thus pointed out the road, that great sage turned back.

sanskrit: upāvṛtte munau tasmin rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt kṛtapuṇyāḥ sma saumitre munir yan no 'nukampate
english: When that sage had turned back, Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa: "We are truly blessed, O son of Sumitrā, that the sage shows such compassion toward us."

sanskrit: iti tau puruṣavyāghrau mantrayitvā manasvinau sītām evāgrataḥ kṛtvā kālindīṃ jagmatur nadīm
english: Having thus taken counsel together, those two tiger-like men, steadfast in mind, placed Sītā ahead of them and proceeded to the river Kālindī.

sanskrit: tau kāṣṭhasaṃghāṭam atho cakratuḥ sumahāplavam cakāra lakṣmaṇaś chittvā sītāyāḥ sukhamānasaṃ
english: Then the two of them assembled a very large raft from logs; Lakṣmaṇa, cutting the timber, fashioned it for Sītā's comfort and peace of mind.

sanskrit: tatra śriyam ivācintyāṃ rāmo dāśarathiḥ priyām īṣatsaṃlajjamānāṃ tām adhyāropayata plavam
english: There Rāma, son of Daśaratha, lifted his beloved — who was like an unimaginable Śrī, slightly bashful — onto the raft.

sanskrit: tataḥ plavenāṃśumatīṃ śīghragām ūrmimālinīm tīrajair bahubhir vṛkṣaiḥ saṃterur yamunāṃ nadīm
english: Then on the raft they crossed the Yamunā — swift-flowing Aṃśumatī, garlanded with waves, its banks lined with many trees.

sanskrit: te tīrṇāḥ plavam utsṛjya prasthāya yamunāvanāt śyāmaṃ nyagrodham āseduḥ śītalaṃ haritacchadam
english: Having crossed, they abandoned the raft and, setting forth from the Yamunā forest, they reached the dark banyan tree, cool and green-leafed.

sanskrit: kausalyāṃ caiva paśyeyaṃ sumitrāṃ ca yaśasvinīm iti sītāñjaliṃ kṛtvā paryagachad vanaspatim
english: "May I see Kausalyā, and glorious Sumitrā as well" — with these words Sītā, folding her hands in reverence, circumambulated the lord of the forest.

sanskrit: krośamātraṃ tato gatvā bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau bahūn medhyān mṛgān hatvā ceratur yamunāvane
english: Having gone just one krośa from there, the two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, slew many pure deer and roamed about in the Yamunā forest.

sanskrit: vihṛtya te barhiṇapūganādite śubhe vane vāraṇavānarāyute samaṃ nadīvapram upetya saṃmataṃ nivāsam ājagmur adīnadarśanaḥ
english: Having sported in the auspicious forest resounding with flocks of peacocks, full of elephants and monkeys, they reached together the bank of the river and came to their appointed campsite — undaunted in bearing.

sanskrit: atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyām avasuptam anantaram prabodhayām āsa śanair lakṣmaṇaṃ raghunandanaḥ
english: When the night had passed and he had slept, the joy of the Raghus gently awakened Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: saumitre śṛṇu vanyānāṃ valgu vyāharatāṃ svanam saṃpratiṣṭhāmahe kālaḥ prasthānasya paraṃtapa
english: "O son of Sumitrā, hear the sweet calls of the forest birds; it is time, O scorcher of foes, to set out on our journey."

sanskrit: sa suptaḥ samaye bhrātrā lakṣmaṇaḥ pratibodhitaḥ jahau nidrāṃ ca tandrīṃ ca prasaktaṃ ca pathi śramam
english: Lakṣmaṇa, who had been sleeping, was roused at the right moment by his brother; he shook off sleep, drowsiness, and the accumulated fatigue of the road.

sanskrit: tata utthāya te sarve spṛṣṭvā nadyāḥ śivaṃ jalam panthānam ṛṣiṇoddiṣṭaṃ citrakūṭasya taṃ yayuḥ
english: Rising then, all of them touched the auspicious water of the river and set out on the path to Citrakūṭa that the sage had pointed out.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃprasthitaḥ kāle rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha sītāṃ kamalapatrākṣīm idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then Rāma, setting forth at the right hour together with the son of Sumitrā, spoke these words to Sītā of lotus-petal eyes.

sanskrit: ādīptān iva vaidehi sarvataḥ puṣpitān nagān svaiḥ puṣpaiḥ kiṃśukān paśya mālinaḥ śiśirātyaye
english: "Behold, O Vaidehī, the trees blazing as if aflame with blossoms all around — the kiṃśuka trees, adorned with their own flowers, as winter draws to its end."

sanskrit: paśya bhallātakān phullān narair anupasevitān phalapatrair avanatān nūnaṃ śakṣyāmi jīvitum
english: "Behold the bhallātaka trees in full bloom, untouched by men, bending low with their fruit and leaves — surely I shall be able to live here."

sanskrit: paśya droṇapramāṇāni lambamānāni lakṣmaṇa madhūni madhukārībhiḥ saṃbhṛtāni nage nage
english: "See, O Lakṣmaṇa, the honeycombs the size of a droṇa measure hanging from tree to tree, filled by the bees."

sanskrit: eṣa krośati natyūhas taṃ śikhī pratikūjati ramaṇīye vanoddeśe puṣpasaṃstarasaṃkaṭe
english: "Here the krauñca cries out, and the peacock calls back to it, in a charming corner of the forest dense with a carpet of flowers."

sanskrit: mātaṃgayūthānusṛtaṃ pakṣisaṃghānunāditam citrakūṭam imaṃ paśya pravṛddhaśikharaṃ girim
english: "Behold this mountain Citrakūṭa, followed by herds of elephants, resounding with flocks of birds, its peaks towering high."

sanskrit: tatas tau pādacāreṇa gacchantau saha sītayā ramyam āsedatuḥ śailaṃ citrakūṭaṃ manoramam
english: Then the two of them, going on foot together with Sītā, reached the charming and lovely mountain Citrakūṭa.

sanskrit: taṃ tu parvatam āsādya nānāpakṣigaṇāyutam ayaṃ vāso bhavet tāvad atra saumya ramemahi
english: Having reached that mountain teeming with diverse flocks of birds, he said: "O gentle one, let this be our dwelling; here let us take our delight for now."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇānaya dārūṇi dṛḍhāni ca varāṇi ca kuruṣvāvasathaṃ saumya vāse me 'bhirataṃ manaḥ
english: "O Lakṣmaṇa, bring strong and excellent timbers and build a shelter, O gentle one — my mind delights in dwelling here."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā saumitrir vividhān drumān ājahāra tataś cakre parṇa śālām ariṃ dama
english: Hearing those words of his, the son of Sumitrā brought various trees and thereupon built a leaf hut, O tamer of foes.

sanskrit: śuśrūṣamāṇam ekāgram idaṃ vacanam abravīt aiṇeyaṃ māṃsam āhṛtya śālāṃ yakṣyāmahe vayam
english: To him who was attentively and single-mindedly at work, Rāma spoke these words: "Having brought the flesh of a black antelope, let us consecrate the hall with sacrifice."

sanskrit: sa lakṣmaṇaḥ kṛṣṇamṛgaṃ hatvā medhyaṃ patāpavān atha cikṣepa saumitriḥ samiddhe jātavedasi
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa of great glory slew a pure black antelope and cast it onto the blazing sacrificial fire.

sanskrit: taṃ tu pakvaṃ samājñāya niṣṭaptaṃ chinnaśoṇitam lakṣmaṇaḥ puruṣavyāghram atha rāghavam abravīt
english: Knowing it to be well cooked, fully roasted, its blood drained, Lakṣmaṇa then spoke to Rāghava, that tiger among men.

sanskrit: ayaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ samāptāṅgaḥ śṛtaḥ kṛṣṇa mṛgo yathā devatā devasaṃkāśa yajasva kuśalo hy asi
english: "This dark one, whole in all its limbs, is cooked — the black antelope is ready. O god-like one, make the offering to the deity; you are skilled in this."

sanskrit: rāmaḥ snātvā tu niyato guṇavāñ japyakovidaḥ pāpasaṃśamanaṃ rāmaś cakāra balim uttamam
english: Rāma, having bathed and composed himself — virtuous, versed in recitation — performed the excellent oblation that pacifies sin.

sanskrit: tāṃ vṛkṣaparṇac chadanāṃ manojñāṃ yathāpradeśaṃ sukṛtāṃ nivātām vāsāya sarve viviśuḥ sametāḥ sabhāṃ yathā deva gaṇāḥ sudharmām
english: Into that leaf-thatched dwelling — pleasing, well built in the right proportions, sheltered from the wind — all of them entered together for the night, as the hosts of gods enter the hall of Sudharmā.

sanskrit: anekanānāmṛgapakṣisaṃkule vicitrapuṣpastabalair drumair yute vanottame vyālamṛgānunādite tathā vijahruḥ susukhaṃ jitendriyāḥ
english: In that excellent forest — swarming with countless diverse beasts and birds, adorned with trees bearing clusters of bright flowers, echoing with wild animals — they, masters of their senses, sported in great delight.

sanskrit: suramyam āsādya tu citrakūṭaṃ nadīṃ ca tāṃ mālyavatīṃ sutīrthām nananda hṛṣṭo mṛgapakṣijuṣṭāṃ jahau ca duḥkhaṃ puravipravāsāt
english: Having reached the supremely lovely Citrakūṭa and the river Mālyavatī with its good fords, teeming with deer and birds, Rāma rejoiced with gladness and left behind the grief of his banishment from the city.

sanskrit: kathayitvā suduḥkhārtaḥ sumantreṇa ciraṃ saha rāme dakṣiṇa kūlasthe jagāma svagṛhaṃ guhaḥ
english: Having spoken at length with Sumantra, deep in sorrow, when Rāma had reached the southern bank, Guha went to his own home.

sanskrit: anujñātaḥ sumantro 'tha yojayitvā hayottamān ayodhyām eva nagarīṃ prayayau gāḍhadurmanāḥ
english: Then Sumantra, having received leave, hitched the excellent horses and departed for the city of Ayodhyā, his heart deeply sorrowful.

sanskrit: sa vanāni sugandhīni saritaś ca sarāṃsi ca paśyann atiyayau śīghraṃ grāmāṇi nagarāṇi ca
english: Beholding fragrant forests, rivers, and lakes, he swiftly passed through villages and towns.

sanskrit: tataḥ sāyāhnasamaye tṛtīye 'hani sārathiḥ ayodhyāṃ samanuprāpya nirānandāṃ dadarśa ha
english: Then at the hour of evening, on the third day, the charioteer reached Ayodhyā and beheld it joyless.

sanskrit: sa śūnyām iva niḥśabdāṃ dṛṣṭvā paramadurmanāḥ sumantraś cintayām āsa śokavegasamāhataḥ
english: Seeing it as though empty and silent, deeply downcast, Sumantra fell to brooding, struck by the force of grief.

sanskrit: kaccin na sagajā sāśvā sajanā sajanādhipā rāmasaṃtāpaduḥkhena dagdhā śokāgninā purī iti cintāparaḥ sūtas tvaritaḥ praviveśa ha
english: "Has the city, with its elephants and horses, its people and its lord, been consumed by the fire of grief, burned by the anguish of sorrow over Rāma?" — so reflecting, the charioteer hastened and entered.

sanskrit: sumantram abhiyāntaṃ taṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ kva rāma iti pṛcchantaḥ sūtam abhyadravan narāḥ
english: Hundreds and thousands of men ran up to Sumantra as he came, asking the charioteer: "Where is Rāma?"

sanskrit: teṣāṃ śaśaṃsa gaṅgāyām aham āpṛcchya rāghavam anujñāto nivṛtto 'smi dhārmikeṇa mahātmanā
english: He reported to them: "At the Gaṅgā I took leave of Rāghava; I was granted leave and turned back by that righteous great soul."

sanskrit: te tīrṇā iti vijñāya bāṣpapūrṇamukhā janāḥ aho dhig iti niḥśvasya hā rāmeti ca cukruśuḥ
english: The people, learning that they had crossed, their faces filled with tears, sighed "Alas!" and cried aloud "O Rāma!"

sanskrit: śuśrāva ca vacas teṣāṃ vṛndaṃ vṛndaṃ ca tiṣṭhatām hatāḥ sma khalu ye neha paśyāma iti rāghavam
english: And he heard the words of those standing in groups: "We are indeed undone, we who cannot see Rāghava here."

sanskrit: dānayajñavivāheṣu samājeṣu mahatsu ca na drakṣyāmaḥ punar jātu dhārmikaṃ rāmam antarā
english: "At gifts and sacrifices, at marriages, at great assemblies — we shall never again see righteous Rāma among us."

sanskrit: kiṃ samarthaṃ janasyāsya kiṃ priyaṃ kiṃ sukhāvaham iti rāmeṇa nagaraṃ pitṛvat paripālitam
english: "What is best for this people, what is pleasing, what brings happiness?" — thus had Rāma tended the city like a father.

sanskrit: vātāyanagatānāṃ ca strīṇām anvantarāpaṇam rāmaśokābhitaptānāṃ śuśrāva paridevanam
english: He also heard the lamentations of women standing at their windows along the streets of the market, scorched by grief for Rāma.

sanskrit: sa rājamārgamadhyena sumantraḥ pihitānanaḥ yatra rājā daśarathas tad evopayayau gṛham
english: Sumantra, covering his face, proceeded along the middle of the royal road to the very palace where King Daśaratha dwelt.

sanskrit: so 'vatīrya rathāc chīghraṃ rājaveśma praviśya ca kakṣyāḥ saptābhicakrāma mahājanasamākulāḥ
english: Swiftly dismounting from the chariot and entering the royal palace, he traversed the seven courts crowded with great throngs of people.

sanskrit: tato daśarathastrīṇāṃ prāsādebhyas tatas tataḥ rāmaśokābhitaptānāṃ mandaṃ śuśrāva jalpitam
english: Then from the palaces here and there he heard the soft murmuring of Daśaratha's women, scorched by grief for Rāma.

sanskrit: saha rāmeṇa niryāto vinā rāmam ihāgataḥ sūtaḥ kiṃ nāma kausalyāṃ śocantīṃ prativakṣyati
english: "The charioteer who went out with Rāma has returned here without Rāma — what shall he ever say to Kausalyā who is mourning?"

sanskrit: yathā ca manye durjīvam evaṃ na sukaraṃ dhruvam ācchidya putre niryāte kausalyā yatra jīvati
english: "And I believe life is hard — truly it is no easy thing — since Kausalyā goes on living when her son has been taken away and sent forth."

sanskrit: satya rūpaṃ tu tadvākyaṃ rājñaḥ strīṇāṃ niśāmayan pradīptam iva śokena viveśa sahasā gṛham
english: Hearing those words of the king's women to be true in every sense, he entered the palace at once, blazing as it were with grief.

sanskrit: sa praviśyāṣṭamīṃ kakṣyāṃ rājānaṃ dīnam ātulam putraśokaparidyūnam apaśyat pāṇḍare gṛhe
english: Entering the eighth court, he saw the king — wretched, incomparable in his anguish, utterly wasted by grief for his son — in the white inner chamber.

sanskrit: abhigamya tam āsīnaṃ narendram abhivādya ca sumantro rāmavacanaṃ yathoktaṃ pratyavedayat
english: Approaching the lord of men as he sat and saluting him, Sumantra reported Rāma's words exactly as they had been spoken.

sanskrit: sa tūṣṇīm eva tac chrutvā rājā vibhrānta cetanaḥ mūrchito nyapatad bhūmau rāmaśokābhipīḍitaḥ
english: Hearing that, the king remained silent; his senses confused, he fainted and fell to the ground, tormented by grief for Rāma.

sanskrit: tato 'ntaḥpuram āviddhaṃ mūrchite pṛthivīpatau uddhṛtya bāhū cukrośa nṛpatau patite kṣitau
english: Then the inner apartments were thrown into commotion when the lord of the earth fainted; when the king fell to the ground, cries arose with arms upraised.

sanskrit: sumitrayā tu sahitā kausalyā patitaṃ patim utthāpayām āsa tadā vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Then Kausalyā, together with Sumitrā, raised her fallen husband and spoke these words.

sanskrit: imaṃ tasya mahābhāga dūtaṃ duṣkarakāriṇaḥ vanavāsād anuprāptaṃ kasmān na pratibhāṣase
english: "O greatly fortunate one, why do you not speak to this messenger of that great doer of difficult deeds, who has arrived from the forest exile?"

sanskrit: adyemam anayaṃ kṛtvā vyapatrapasi rāghava uttiṣṭha sukṛtaṃ te 'stu śoke na syāt sahāyatā
english: "Today, having done this wrong to him, you are ashamed, O Rāghava; arise — may it go well with you; grief is no fitting companion."

sanskrit: deva yasyā bhayād rāmaṃ nānupṛcchasi sārathim neha tiṣṭhati kaikeyī viśrabdhaṃ pratibhāṣyatām
english: "O lord, Kaikeyī, through fear of whom you do not question the charioteer about Rāma — she is not here; speak freely with confidence."

sanskrit: sā tathoktvā mahārājaṃ kausalyā śokalālasā dharaṇyāṃ nipapātāśu bāṣpaviplutabhāṣiṇī
english: Having spoken thus to the great king, Kausalyā, overcome with grief, swiftly fell to the earth, her speech dissolved in tears.

sanskrit: evaṃ vilapatīṃ dṛṣṭvā kausalyāṃ patitāṃ bhuvi patiṃ cāvekṣya tāḥ sarvāḥ sasvaraṃ ruruduḥ striyaḥ
english: Seeing Kausalyā lamenting thus and fallen to the ground, and looking at the king, all those women wept aloud.

sanskrit: tatas tam antaḥpuranādam utthitaṃ samīkṣya vṛddhās taruṇāś ca mānavāḥ striyaś ca sarvā ruruduḥ samantataḥ puraṃ tadāsīt punar eva saṃkulam
english: Then, hearing that cry that rose from the inner apartments, the old and the young, men and all women, wept on every side; the city was once again thrown into tumult.
